text:
MacKenzie Weegar is having the kind of season that looks better the closer you watch. In his first full year with Utah after coming over from Calgary, he's playing 22 minutes a night, has thrown 71 hits and blocked 65 shots, and at five on five the Mammoth have taken almost 60% of the expected goals (the quality of their chances) with him on the ice. That is dominant territorial play from a top-pair defenseman.

The points don't show it: 6 in 25 games, none on the power play, 2 in his last ten. The reason is mostly at the other end of the ice. Utah has scored 13.1 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Weegar out there, the kind of gap that usually swings back. Evolving-Hockey had a rough read on his 2025-26 (below replacement, with penalties costing him), though it also found he was better than his goals. Our numbers project about 25 points. For a seventh-round pick with more than 600 NHL games behind him, the job is the minutes, and he has them. Watch whether Utah's finishing catches up to what he's helping build.
headline: MacKenzie Weegar is winning the ice, not the scoresheet
